Williams & Associates, PLC, For Your Free ConsultationWhat Is The Difference Between Getting Arrested By Manassas City Police Versus Prince William County Police? The Manassas City Police Department and the Prince William County Police Department are separate law enforcement agencies. Each one has its own jurisdiction and authority. If police arrest you within Manassas city limits, the Manassas City Police Department usually handles the arrest and investigation. City officers make the arrest, prepare the charges and begin the case. Even though Manassas is an independent city, most criminal cases still move through the Prince William County court system. This overlap often confuses people who have never dealt with the local courts before. If police arrest you outside Manassas city limits, the Prince William County Police Department usually handles the case. The arresting agency can affect where officers take you, how they process your charges and what happens during the early stages of your case. Knowing which agency made the arrest helps your attorney act quickly and protect your rights from the start. What Types Of Criminal Charges Can Our Manassas Defense Lawyers Handle? Our Manassas criminal lawyers handle a wide range of criminal offenses, including both felony offenses and misdemeanor charges. We represent clients facing serious criminal charges that can result in significant potential penalties, including jail time, fines and a permanent criminal record. Whether you face minor infractions or serious felonies, our experienced team provides comprehensive legal representation throughout the legal process. Drug Charges Drug crimes encompass various violations of Virginia’s controlled substance laws under Virginia Code Section 18.2-248. Our attorneys defend clients against the following drug-related charges. Drug possession Drug distribution Drug trafficking Prescription fraud These drug offenses can result in years of imprisonment, substantial fines and permanent criminal conviction records that affect future employment and housing opportunities. DUI And DWI Virginia law defines driving under the influence (DUI) and driving while intoxicated (DWI) under Virginia Code Section 18.2-266. Our DUI defense attorney team handles cases involving alcohol, drugs or controlled substances that impair driving ability. We represent repeat offenders facing enhanced penalties, underage drivers with zero-tolerance violations and individuals charged with felony offenses involving serious injury or death. Penalties include license suspension, jail time, substantial fines, mandatory alcohol education programs and ignition interlock device requirements. Sex Crimes Sex crimes carry severe social stigma and harsh legal consequences, requiring immediate legal representation. Our attorneys defend against the following charges: Internet sex crimes Indecent exposure Possession of child pornography Child sex abuse Date rape and acquaintance rape Internet solicitation of a minor Sex offense convictions result in lengthy prison sentences, lifetime sex offender registration and permanent restrictions on residence and employment. Traffic Violations Virginia defines traffic violations under various statutes governing motor vehicle operation. Common violations we handle include: Speeding Reckless driving Traffic tickets Many seemingly minor traffic violations can result in significant potential penalties, requiring experienced traffic violation representation in Manassas to minimize consequences. Violent Crimes Violent crimes involve physical force or threats against other persons, often carrying severe penalties under Virginia law: Homicide/murder Weapons charges Domestic violence These charges require immediate legal attention to protect your rights and build effective defense strategies. White Collar Crimes White collar criminal offenses involve financial gain through nonviolent means: Fraud Embezzlement These charges often involve complex financial evidence requiring thorough investigation and skilled legal guidance. What Are Your Rights After An Arrest In Manassas, Virginia? After an arrest, you have fundamental constitutional rights that must be protected throughout the criminal justice legal process. These include: Right to remain silent Right to legal counsel Right to reasonable bail Right to due process Understanding and exercising these rights immediately after arrest is crucial to protecting your interests. What Are Hot Spots For Traffic Tickets In Manassas, Virginia? Police closely monitor certain roads and intersections in Manassas due to traffic volume, safety concerns and accident history. Common traffic enforcement hot spots include: Route 28 (Center Street/Prescott Avenue): Officers often enforce speed limits along this busy route, especially during morning and evening traffic. Sudley Road (Route 234): Heavy traffic and frequent congestion make this road a common area for speeding and reckless driving tickets. Liberia Avenue: Several intersections use photo red light enforcement, including Liberia Avenue & Centreville Road and Liberia Avenue & Signal Hill Road. These cameras regularly issue citations. Grant Avenue and Center Street: Police monitor this intersection due to steady traffic and safety concerns near nearby neighborhoods and businesses. Drivers often underestimate the seriousness of tickets issued in these areas. When Should You Hire A Manassas Criminal Defense Attorney? Early intervention allows your attorney to protect your rights, prevent self-incrimination and begin building your defense. Having experienced legal representation provides numerous benefits, including knowledge of local court procedures, relationships with prosecutors and judges and the ability to negotiate favorable plea agreements or prepare for trial when necessary. Planning for parking can make your court day less stressful. The Lee Avenue Parking Garage offers one of the most convenient options for court visitors. It sits near the Prince William County courthouse complex on Lee Avenue and provides public parking within walking distance of both court buildings. Arrive early when possible. Parking availability can change quickly based on court schedules and the number of hearings scheduled that day.
